heard: a cosmic structure 10 billion light years long shouldn't exist. In 2013, astronomers led by Istvan Horvath mapped the locations of massive stellar explosions called gamma-ray bursts. Using NASA's Swift satellite, the team discovered a strange clustering toward the constellation Hercules. These bursts revealed a hidden superstructure spanning roughly 10 billion light years, one-tenth of the entire observable universe. It is so immense that it defies our core law that matter is evenly spread through space. This record breaker's name was actually coined by a Filipino teenager on Wikipedia, not the discovering scientists. Critics argue it could be a statistical illusion, leaving the structure's true reality to be proven by future telescopes. Our best maps of the early universe suggest that a cosmic structure 10 billion light years long shouldn't exist.
